findings.name: leg examination
findings.result: Right calf red and swollen compared with the left; muscle contours normal; no ulcers or pigmentation. Right leg warmer than the left; pitting pedal edema on the right; multiple healing cuts on the right leg, covered with a bandage; dorsalis pedis pulses palpable and equal on both sides; normal mobility at the ankle, knee and hip.

findings.name: Homans sign
findings.result: Pain in the right calf when the right ankle is dorsiflexed.

other_considerations.note: Injury can cause intramuscular or intermuscular bleeding with pain, swelling and restricted movement, and may lead to posterior compartment syndrome.
Sudden pain at the musculotendinous junction halfway between knee and heel, possibly with bruising, pain on tiptoe and pain on resisted ankle dorsiflexion.
Undue strain can tear muscles or tendons, causing spasm and pain; ligaments can be torn by overstretching or injury.

x008: Source reads '~ BS x 4 quadrants'; '~' is a garbled '+' (bowel sounds present).
x010: The note exam says 'no Homans sign on the right side'; the SP is told to show calf pain on dorsiflexion of the right ankle, and gold diagnosis #1 lists 'Homans sign'. The simulated finding is the result (CONVERSION.md), worded as the SP shows it.
x009: Gold diagnoses describe a 'tender' right calf, but neither the note exam nor the SP notes record calf tenderness on palpation.

leakage.reason: 'My dad had a clot in his leg' is a lay description of DVT, the rank-1 diagnosis (legitimate family history, also in the challenging question).

source_issues: Homans sign conflict: the note exam says 'no Homans sign on the right side', while the SP is told to show calf pain when the right ankle is dorsiflexed and gold diagnosis #1 lists 'Homans sign' as a supporting exam finding. The simulated calf pain on dorsiflexion is the Homans record (x010).
Gold diagnoses #1-#3 describe a 'tender' right calf, but the note exam records no calf tenderness on palpation.

p009 asks about swelling; the answer (legs feel heavy with pressure at the end of the day, both legs) neither confirms nor denies swelling. The note HPI says the pain is 'associated with swelling', and the exam records a swollen right calf.

Gold #2 lists 'Low-grade fever' as a history finding; the patient only felt warm and did not measure her temperature. The doorway temperature is 99.9°F and the note says 'low-grade fever' without a value.
e005: '~ BS x 4 quadrants' is a garbled symbol (probably '+'); recorded as present with a flag (x008).
e006 ('Extremities:') and e009 ('Neuro:') are header-only lines with no findings; listed in excluded_exam_lines.
The note HPI says the pain is aggravated by dorsiflexion of the foot; this is not in the script's exacerbating-factors answer (walking, extending the knee) but matches the SP notes.
The note FH adds 'No history of sudden deaths in the family', which is not in the script (added as flagged note-only fact f037).
p020: 'I use three to four pads' does not say whether per day or per period.
p032 topic is 'Drug allergies/herbal medication', but herbal medicines are never asked about.
The raw sheet's 'Closure' section contains unrelated text about exam-day logistics (arrival time, ID, scratch paper); it was not used.
notes: Ibuprofen use (medication, f033) and its effect (relief, in f008) are recorded separately, as the example does for antacids and Maalox.
Swelling was not inferred from the heaviness/pressure answer (f010, flagged).
The 50-lb weight gain since her last delivery 3 years ago is coded current, since nothing says it was lost.
'Married with two children' from the SP-sheet patient description is in acting_notes (no valid source id); it agrees with 'my spouse' and 'two kids'.

The calf pain on dorsiflexion is worded as the SP shows it, not labeled a positive Homans sign, because the note explicitly records no Homans sign; as the simulated finding it is the result of the Homans record (x010), replacing v1's separate note and SP records (x018, x025).

Conversion: v1 f008 (ibuprofen eases the pain) and f009 (propping the leg up eases it) answer one question and form one relieving list (f008). v1 f002 (worse; mild at first, now with the slightest movement) is the course child f003.

Conversion: the 15-hour flight a week ago (v1 subtype exposures) and frequent work travel (v1 subtype social) are habit_exposure (travel). Oral contraceptives (p019) are a medication parent f034 with the 2-year duration as a child.

Conversion: inspection (e007) and palpation (e008) of the leg form one leg-examination record x009, with the SP's bandage; the Homans sign is its own record (named special test). The note's 'VS: WNL except for low-grade fever' (e002) agrees with the doorway values (99.9°F) and is cited on all four doorway records.
Harmonisation pass: scale [0, 10] added to f005; f030 item -> 'chronic medical problems' (blanket denial).
